current_text.html: It is the duty of the deacons to minister to those who are in need, to the sick, to the friendless, and to any who may be in distress. It is their duty also to develop the grace of liberality in the members of the church, to devise effective methods of collecting the gifts of the people, and to distribute these gifts among the objects to which they are contributed. They shall have the care of the property of the congregation, both real and personal, and shall keep in proper repair the church edifice and other buildings belonging to the congregation. In matters of special importance affecting the property of the church, they cannot take final action without the approval of the Session and consent of the congregation. In the discharge of their duties the deacons are under the supervision and authority of the Session. In a church in which it is impossible for any reason to secure deacons, the duties of the office shall devolve upon the ruling elders.

relationships.title: Requiring session and diaconate membership reporting in RAO 16

metadata.summary: The CCB found an overture amending RAO 16 to mandate statistical reporting on session and diaconate membership and duties to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions.

relationships.title: Unordained Men and Women Carrying Out Diaconal Ministry

metadata.summary: CCB found an overture appointing unordained persons to diaconal ministry in conflict with the Constitution, including because it implied an unordained office contrary to BCO 17-1.
CCB advised that deacons, subject to session approval and congregational consent, hold authority to sell church property such as donated stock.

relationships.title: Reese and Bech v. Philadelphia Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: We believe the language of "for any reason" as presently stated [BCO 9-2 impossible for any reason] gives us needed freedom to exercise our conscience regarding the teaching of scripture that included women within the office of deacon.

metadata.synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery declared Reese and Bech's complaint out of order because some supporting reasons and requested amends allegedly violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding Presbytery misapplied Robert's Rules: objectionable parts do not justify rejecting an entire complaint, and a court need not adopt requested amends. It also said pertinent questions about whether a call is for the good of the Church may be asked, but agreed the amends—including removing TE Hsu—were inappropriate and could not rescind his installation.

metadata.synopsis: Joined with Case 2009-25; the Session of Grace Presbyterian Church complained that views 3, 4, 5, and 6 in Northern California Presbytery's resolution on diaconal practice violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint on the same grounds as 2009-25, annulling the abstract resolution while declining to rule on the constitutional merits of any specific diaconal view.
